paragraphs: Training large language models requires memory for both optimizer states and activations. Methods that reduce only the optimizer’s storage can leave a substantial obstacle when training uses long sequences or large batches. This paper introduces Randomized Subspace Optimization to address both sources of memory use within one training framework.

The method breaks a high-dimensional optimization problem into a succession of smaller problems. At each iteration, it chooses a random subspace and optimizes parameters within that subspace. This changes the scope of each update, allowing the method to reduce activation memory alongside optimizer-state memory. The framework supports both pre-training and fine-tuning.

The authors establish convergence guarantees and rates across several scenarios, including different ways of solving the smaller optimization problems. Their experiments report better memory and communication efficiency while achieving performance comparable to GaLore and Adam. The contribution therefore combines resource savings with theoretical analysis of the training procedure, rather than relying solely on empirical evidence that smaller updates work.
icml-2025-a-memory-efficient-randomized-.tldr: Randomized Subspace Optimization reduces activation and optimizer-state memory while matching GaLore and Adam performance in reported experiments.

paragraphs: Proteins often perform their biological roles through interactions with other proteins or biomolecules. Modeling a single protein chain therefore addresses only part of the problem. This paper introduces APM, an all-atom generative model developed specifically for proteins containing multiple chains and for the interactions that hold protein complexes together.

APM combines atom-level information with training data on multi-chain proteins. The authors report that this enables precise modeling of interactions between chains and the generation of protein complexes with binding capabilities from scratch. The model also supports multi-chain folding and inverse folding, connecting the tasks of determining structures and designing sequences within the same modeling approach.

The paper further evaluates APM in downstream applications. Supervised fine-tuning improves its performance, while certain tasks also support zero-shot sampling, with state-of-the-art results reported. These findings position APM as a versatile approach to multi-chain protein modeling. The central advance is its explicit treatment of atomic detail and interactions across chains, bringing complex design into the model’s scope.
icml-2025-an-all-atom-generative-model-f.tldr: APM uses atom-level information to model multi-chain proteins and generate protein complexes with binding capabilities.

paragraphs: Quantization helps make large language models deployable in environments with limited resources, but it may also weaken their safety capabilities. Earlier evidence focused on a few methods that do not require calibration datasets. This paper broadens the investigation to mainstream quantization techniques and multiple calibration datasets, using established safety benchmarks.

The authors pair this evaluation with Q-resafe, a framework for repairing the safety vulnerabilities they identify. Its patching procedure accounts for quantization and aims to restore safety efficiently while minimizing harm to the model’s usefulness. This makes the relationship between compression, safety, and utility central to the proposed intervention.

Across extensive experiments, the authors report that Q-resafe brings quantized models’ safety back into alignment with their pre-quantization counterparts, including under challenging evaluation conditions. The findings support evaluating safety after quantization and show that targeted repair can recover the evaluated capabilities. The comparison is specifically with the original models’ safety behavior, so the reported achievement is restoration of that reference level.
icml-2025-assessing-safety-risks-and-qua.tldr: Q-resafe repairs safety weaknesses in quantized language models, restoring evaluated safety toward pre-quantization levels while minimizing utility loss.

paragraphs: Online knowledge distillation trains teacher and student models within one process, avoiding the need for a separately pretrained teacher. This paper examines intermediate spatial features as a source of knowledge transfer. Its analysis finds that features shared by teachers and students concentrate mainly on foreground objects, and that teachers emphasize those objects more strongly.

The proposed Asymmetric Decision-Making method gives the two models different learning priorities. Students emphasize spatial features that already show strong agreement with teachers. Teachers emphasize features with lower similarity to students, which the authors associate with stronger teacher performance in those regions. Agreement guides the student while divergence encourages the teacher to retain distinct strengths.

This arrangement is intended to help students catch up with teachers’ feature learning without making both models pursue identical representations. Experiments report consistent improvements over existing online distillation methods across multiple settings. The approach also transfers successfully to offline distillation, semantic segmentation, and diffusion distillation, supporting the usefulness of assigning complementary roles to consensus and diversity.
icml-2025-asymmetric-decision-making-in-.tldr: ADM improves knowledge distillation by encouraging students to learn shared spatial features while teachers develop distinct feature strengths.

paragraphs: Vision-language models combine visual perception with language-based capabilities such as reasoning, but how these abilities interact remains unclear. This paper investigates that interaction by merging model parameters across modalities. Its practical goal is to bring reasoning capabilities from language models into vision-language models without additional training.

The experiments demonstrate successful reasoning transfer through this merging procedure. The authors also use the resulting models to investigate where perception and reasoning are represented across layers. Before merging, perception is predominantly associated with early layers, while reasoning depends largely on middle and later layers. These are observed concentrations of capability, rather than strict boundaries separating the two functions.

After merging, the authors observe contributions to reasoning across all layers, while the layerwise distribution of perception remains largely unchanged. This suggests that merging can alter how reasoning is distributed without similarly reorganizing perception. The work therefore presents model merging both as a practical route to multimodal capability transfer and as a way to study how those capabilities coexist.
icml-2025-bring-reason-to-vision-underst.tldr: Cross-modal model merging transfers language-model reasoning into vision-language models without training and reveals changes in layerwise reasoning contributions.

paragraphs: Consistency models aim to generate data directly from noise, enabling one-step sampling while allowing additional steps to improve quality. This paper studies when their generated distribution approaches the target distribution. Crucially, the analysis allows self-consistency to hold approximately under the training distribution, rather than requiring exact agreement.

The guarantees depend on properties of the target data. If its support is bounded, or its tails decay sufficiently quickly, the authors establish closeness in Wasserstein distance, a measure that accounts for how far probability mass must move. Under a smoothness assumption, an additional smoothing perturbation enables a guarantee in total variation distance, which compares probabilities assigned to events.

The analysis applies to a family of forward processes and includes two case studies using common choices to demonstrate benefits from multistep sampling. Its contribution is to connect approximate learned consistency with distributional guarantees under stated data conditions. The results also explain why taking multiple sampling steps can be valuable within a framework designed to permit direct generation.
icml-2025-convergence-of-consistency-mod.tldr: The paper establishes conditional distributional convergence guarantees for approximately consistent models and demonstrates benefits of multistep sampling.

paragraphs: As language-model contexts become very long, attention must handle increasing amounts of potentially redundant information. This adds computation and storage costs and can also weaken representations. Core Context Aware Attention addresses this problem by combining a compressed view of the broader context with a detailed view of nearby tokens.

Its global module groups input tokens and dynamically summarizes each group into one core token according to token significance. This is designed to emphasize useful context while reducing redundancy. A complementary local module incorporates neighboring tokens, preserving information needed for detailed representations. Together, the modules address long-range dependencies and local detail through different parts of the attention mechanism.

The authors present CCA-Attention as a replacement for self-attention in existing language models that requires minimal fine-tuning. Their experiments report advantages over state-of-the-art methods in both long-context modeling and computational efficiency. The findings support the idea that selectively compressing broader context can improve efficiency while retaining a separate path for information that benefits from finer resolution.
icml-2025-core-context-aware-transformer.tldr: CCA-Attention combines significance-based context compression with nearby-token detail to improve long-context modeling and efficiency.

paragraphs: Diffusion models face computational costs that make scaling difficult, particularly when their architectures treat every generation stage and spatial token uniformly. Diff-MoE combines Diffusion Transformers with a mixture of experts to make processing responsive to both the current stage of generation and the spatial content being handled.

Each expert receives its own timestep conditioning, allowing it to adapt to the generative stage while processing different spatial tokens. The framework can therefore allocate resources according to temporal and spatial characteristics together. It also introduces a globally informed feature recalibration mechanism, which adjusts the contributions of features according to their relevance to the input.

Experiments on image-generation benchmarks report significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods. The stated findings support the potential of expert-based architectures to provide a more flexible foundation for diffusion generation. The main architectural contribution is the combination of stage-aware experts, spatially adaptive processing, and feature recalibration, all directed toward improving representation and resource allocation within the generative model.
icml-2025-diff-moe-diffusion-transformer.tldr: Diff-MoE improves diffusion image generation with experts that adapt to generation timesteps, spatial tokens, and input-relevant features.

paragraphs: Reward models can judge an entire answer or provide finer feedback during its construction. Token-level feedback offers detailed credit assignment, but deriving rewards from generation probabilities mixes language generation with reward modeling. The authors argue that these objectives can conflict, causing unstable training and inaccurate judgments about individual tokens.

Their Q-function Reward Model separates reward modeling from generation by optimizing a discriminative policy. The theoretical result shows that Q-RM explicitly learns token-level Q-functions from preference data without needing fine-grained annotations. This connects relatively coarse preferences to detailed reward signals that can guide policy optimization.

Across the reported benchmarks, Q-RM outperforms all evaluated baselines. With PPO and REINFORCE, average mathematical-reasoning Pass@1 improves by 5.85 and 4.70 points over outcome rewards, and by 4.56 and 5.73 points over the token-level process-reward comparison. Training also converges 12 times faster than the outcome model on GSM8K and 11 times faster than the step-level model on MATH. These results link improved reward assignment with both stronger answers and faster training in the evaluated settings.
icml-2025-discriminative-policy-optimiza.tldr: Q-RM learns token-level rewards from preferences independently of language generation, improving reasoning performance and training speed in reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Vision Transformers can estimate three-dimensional poses, but image-based architectures lack temporal information and may produce predictions that do not align well with image pixels. ExtPose extends these models to incorporate additional two-dimensional pose evidence and information across video frames, aiming for more consistent three-dimensional predictions.

The method represents structured pose evidence using images of human skeletons. It then uses attention across modalities and frames to connect this evidence with the visual input and temporal context. Parameter sharing allows these extensions without adding parameters. The design brings spatial structure and temporal information into a common attention-based framework.

The authors report state-of-the-art results on multiple human and hand pose benchmarks. Against other ViT-based methods, PA-MPJPE reaches 34.0 millimeters on 3DPW and 4.9 millimeters on FreiHAND, improvements of 23% and 18%, respectively. These results support the value of supplementing image representations with structured pose evidence and cross-frame attention to improve estimated poses and their consistency with the underlying visual observations.
icml-2025-extpose-robust-and-coherent-po.tldr: ExtPose adds structured 2D pose evidence and temporal attention to ViTs without extra parameters, improving human and hand pose estimation.

paragraphs: Time-series classifiers often encounter test data whose distribution differs from their training data, which can substantially reduce accuracy. Normalization methods that help time-series regression have been less satisfactory for classification. FIC-TSC addresses this challenge through a constraint on training, with the aim of improving generalization under distribution shifts.

The framework uses Fisher information as its constraint. The authors provide theoretical and empirical evidence that this guides optimization toward flatter minima: solutions in regions where changes to parameters have a less sharp effect on the training objective. Their analysis connects this training behavior to improved ability to handle changes in the data distribution.

Evaluation covers 30 multivariate datasets from UEA and 85 univariate datasets from UCR, with comparisons against 14 recent state-of-the-art methods. The reported results favor FIC-TSC across this evaluation. The contribution is a training framework that ties a specific information-based constraint to optimization geometry and then tests whether that connection translates into stronger time-series classification performance.
icml-2025-fic-tsc-learning-time-series-c.tldr: FIC-TSC uses a Fisher-information constraint to encourage flatter solutions and improve time-series classification under distribution shifts.

paragraphs: Standard diffusion and flow-matching formulations use a single Gaussian description, predicting either its mean or a corresponding flow velocity. The paper identifies two difficulties: errors when generation uses few sampling steps and oversaturated colors under classifier-free guidance. GMFlow addresses these through a richer probabilistic description of the generation process.

Instead of predicting one mean, GMFlow predicts changing Gaussian-mixture parameters to represent a flow-velocity distribution with multiple modes. Training uses a KL-divergence loss. The authors show that this formulation generalizes previous single-Gaussian models trained with a squared-error denoising loss, placing those models within the broader framework.

For generation, the paper derives stochastic and deterministic solvers that use analytic denoising distributions and velocity fields. A probabilistic guidance scheme also reduces the oversaturation associated with classifier-free guidance. Experiments consistently favor GMFlow over flow-matching baselines, including a reported Precision of 0.942 with six sampling steps on ImageNet at 256 by 256 resolution. The results support combining richer distributions with solvers and guidance designed to use them.
icml-2025-gaussian-mixture-flow-matching.tldr: GMFlow predicts Gaussian-mixture flow distributions and uses tailored solvers and guidance to improve few-step image generation.

paragraphs: A central theoretical question is how neural networks can substantially change their learned features while still reaching globally optimal solutions. Analyses based on neural tangent kernels keep features close to initialization, limiting what they explain about richer representation learning. This paper studies infinitely wide, multilayer networks in a different parameterization.

Using the tensor-program framework, the authors analyze stochastic gradient descent under Maximal Update parameterization. Under mild conditions on the activation function, they show that training learns linearly independent features that move substantially away from their initial values. The analysis uses interactions between layers and properties of Gaussian random variables to characterize this evolving representation.

The resulting feature space captures relevant data information and ensures that any convergent point of training is a global minimum. This is a statement about points to which training converges; it does not by itself assert that every training trajectory converges. Experiments on real-world datasets support the theoretical findings, connecting substantial feature evolution with favorable optimization properties in the studied infinite-width setting.
icml-2025-global-convergence-and-rich-fe.tldr: Under stated conditions, infinite-width networks with Maximal Update parameterization learn rich features and have globally optimal convergent training points.

paragraphs: Representing a molecule as tokens for individual graph nodes can overlook meaningful structure at larger scales. Functional groups carry biochemical information that is not explicitly represented by an atom-only view. This paper links the omission of molecular hierarchy to weaker molecule-language alignment and severe hallucination in language-model outputs.

HIGHT introduces a graph tokenizer that represents three levels together: atoms, motifs, and whole molecules. These tokens give the language model access to both local components and broader molecular organization. The approach also enriches its instruction-tuning dataset with hierarchical graph information, so the training examples reinforce the structure exposed by the tokenizer.

Experiments across 14 real-world benchmarks report a 40% reduction in hallucination and significant gains on multiple molecule-language tasks. The findings support treating molecular hierarchy as useful semantic information during both representation and instruction tuning. The paper’s contribution is therefore a coordinated change to how molecules are presented to language models and how the models learn to connect those representations with language.
icml-2025-hierarchical-graph-tokenizatio.tldr: HIGHT represents atoms, motifs, and whole molecules together, improving molecule-language tasks and reducing hallucination by 40% in reported experiments.

paragraphs: Batch normalization becomes difficult in federated learning because different clients can have different data distributions. Means and variances estimated across these clients need a coherent update procedure. Standard batch normalization can otherwise degrade performance. Hybrid Batch Normalisation addresses this by reworking how statistical information is maintained and used.

HBN separates updates to statistical parameters, such as evaluation means and variances, from gradient-based updates to learnable parameters. This separation produces unbiased estimates of global statistics in distributed settings. A learnable mixing factor then lets each computing node combine statistics from its current batch with global statistics, adapting the balance to the node.

The approach emphasizes that global information can support learning even when clients have heterogeneous data. Experiments show promising results across a broad range of federated settings, with particular benefits for small batches and heterogeneous distributions. HBN is presented as a plugin layer, making the normalization mechanism itself the intervention rather than requiring an entirely new federated learning system.
icml-2025-hybrid-batch-normalisation-res.tldr: HBN improves federated normalization by separating statistical updates and learning how to mix local batch statistics with global estimates.

paragraphs: Neural networks can be trained to solve partial differential equations, but singularly perturbed equations create a particularly difficult optimization problem. Certain equation parameters introduce near-singular behavior in the loss function. This paper addresses that source of training difficulty through a method based on homotopy dynamics.

The method manipulates the troublesome parameters through the proposed dynamics, making their treatment part of the optimization strategy. The authors analyze how these parameters affect training difficulty and establish convergence of their method. This connects the mathematical source of the difficulty with the mechanism intended to overcome it, giving the approach a theoretical foundation.

Experiments report significantly faster convergence and more accurate solutions for the singularly perturbed problems studied. The findings indicate that managing the perturbation parameters can improve neural-network solvers where the original training objective is difficult to optimize. The contribution is an optimization framework for this class of differential equations, supported by both convergence analysis and empirical improvements in speed and accuracy.
icml-2025-learn-singularly-perturbed-sol.tldr: A homotopy-dynamics method manages difficult PDE parameters, with convergence theory and reported gains in neural-solver speed and accuracy.

paragraphs: Multi-objective optimization involves balancing several objectives, and practical algorithms often rely on application-specific tuning. Choosing settings from observed problem instances is common, but the resulting choices usually lack theoretical guarantees. This paper treats algorithm configuration as a learning problem and asks when performance on sampled instances can generalize.

The authors establish generalization guarantees for selecting parameters of multi-objective optimization algorithms using sampled problems. They also give a stronger result for a particular performance measure, Pareto volume: an approximately optimal configuration can be learned in polynomial time within the probably approximately correct framework. That computational guarantee is explicitly tied to the stated choice of metric.

The framework is applied to approximation algorithms, local search, and linear programming, with experiments on multiple problems supporting the theory. Its significance is to give data-driven tuning a formal foundation. Instead of treating successful parameter settings as merely empirical discoveries, the analysis identifies settings in which learning a configuration comes with guarantees about its quality and generalization.
icml-2025-learning-configurations-for-da.tldr: The paper gives generalization guarantees for tuning multi-objective algorithms and polynomial-time learning guarantees when performance is measured by Pareto volume.

paragraphs: Training on short problems and succeeding on longer ones requires handling aspects of scale that training may not expose. This paper formalizes that challenge as generalization from a lower-dimensional subspace to a higher-dimensional space. The connection assumes that instances arise from latent variables representing problem scale.

The authors show that this form of generalization requires an appropriate inductive bias. For Boolean functions, different architectures trained by gradient descent or stochastic gradient descent favor minimum-degree interpolators relative to different linearly independent sets. Successful generalization depends on alignment between the target function and the architecture’s resulting bias, rather than simply fitting the training examples.

The paper uses this perspective to explain chain-of-thought reasoning as restructuring the latent space in a way that improves generalization across dimensions. It also proposes treating scale generalization and data-format effects separately when designing positional embeddings. Following this principle, RPE-Square extends relative positional embeddings to handle data formats better. The contribution connects a theoretical account of generalization with concrete representation-design choices.
icml-2025-low-dimension-to-high-dimensio.tldr: The paper links length generalization to inductive bias in higher-dimensional extrapolation and uses that perspective to motivate RPE-Square embeddings.

paragraphs: OmniArch explores whether a unified foundation-model approach can support scientific computing across multiple scales, physical systems, and spatial dimensions. The paper presents a prototype that combines shared pre-training with physics-informed adaptation, aiming to bring these requirements together in one architecture.

During pre-training, a Fourier encoder-decoder addresses differences across dimensions, while a Transformer backbone integrates quantities through their temporal dynamics. A separate PDE-Aligner provides physics-informed fine-tuning under flexible conditions. These components assign complementary roles to representing scientific data, learning its evolution, and adapting the model in accordance with physical information.

The authors report joint pre-training across one-, two-, and three-dimensional problems on PDEBench, describing it as a first to their knowledge. They report new performance benchmarks in all three dimensional settings and adaptability to new physics through in-context and zero-shot learning. The findings support the prototype’s ambition to share capabilities across scientific problems, with engineering applications and physics discovery presented as potential uses of that broader adaptability.
icml-2025-omniarch-building-foundation-m.tldr: OmniArch combines joint multidimensional PDE pre-training with physics-informed adaptation to support scientific computing across scales and physical systems.

paragraphs: Actor-critic methods are widely used in continuous control, but much of their theoretical analysis focuses on simplified settings. These include finite state and action spaces, separate update loops, or independently sampled data. This paper studies a formulation closer to common practice: single-timescale updates in continuous spaces with Markovian sampling.

In this setting, the actor and critic evolve together, while samples retain the dependence associated with a Markov process. The authors introduce a Lyapunov analysis framework that characterizes convergence of both components jointly. This allows their interaction to be treated as part of the central mathematical problem.

The paper establishes finite-time convergence and describes the analysis as less conservative than previous approaches. Its main contribution is theoretical: it provides a unified account of the coupled learning dynamics under the stated update and sampling setup. By addressing continuous spaces and dependent sampling together, the result strengthens the connection between actor-critic convergence analysis and the algorithms commonly used for continuous-control applications.
icml-2025-on-the-convergence-of-continuo.tldr: A joint Lyapunov analysis establishes finite-time convergence for single-timescale actor-critic updates in continuous spaces with Markovian sampling.

paragraphs: Text watermarks introduce statistical patterns during language-model generation so detectors can recognize outputs from a specified model. Many methods place these signals in high-entropy token choices to preserve text quality. This paper shows that the same design choice can expose a shared weakness in watermark robustness.

The proposed Self-Information Rewrite Attack uses token self-information to identify likely carriers of watermark patterns and directs paraphrasing toward them. The approach does not require access to the watermarking algorithm or the model that produced the watermarked text. The authors also report that it can transfer across language models used for rewriting, including mobile-level models.

Experiments achieve nearly 100% attack success against seven recent watermarking methods, at a reported cost of $0.88 per million tokens. These findings demonstrate a substantial vulnerability across the evaluated methods, rather than establishing that every possible watermark can be removed. The broader implication is that a design intended to protect writing quality can create a recognizable target for edits, motivating more robust watermark designs.
icml-2025-revealing-weaknesses-in-text-w.tldr: SIRA exposes a shared weakness in seven evaluated text-watermarking methods through inexpensive, targeted paraphrasing without access to the watermarking system.

paragraphs: Long videos are expensive for vision-language models to process, and compressing their representations can discard temporal relationships or important meaning. ViLAMP addresses this through differential distillation: preserving information relevant to the task while removing redundancy. Its hierarchy makes separate decisions about which frames and which within-frame features to retain.

First, differential keyframe selection favors frames that are relevant to the query while remaining temporally distinct. Second, feature merging preserves query-relevant patches in the remaining frames. Keyframes retain full information, while non-keyframes receive a more compressed representation. The paper compares this unequal allocation of detail to mixed precision, with different parts of the video receiving different representational treatment.

Experiments across five video-understanding benchmarks report superior performance, especially on long-form content. The authors demonstrate processing up to 10,000 frames on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU while maintaining state-of-the-art performance. The results support selective, query-aware preservation at both frame and patch levels as a way to extend video coverage without uniformly retaining every detail.
icml-2025-scaling-video-language-models-.tldr: ViLAMP preserves query-relevant frames and features to process videos up to 10,000 frames on one A100 GPU with strong benchmark performance.

paragraphs: A multimodal model may encounter a change in only one of its input sources while the others remain stable. This paper studies that specific test-time adaptation problem. It matters because applying adaptation across a combined model must account for the unequal effects of a distribution shift on its different modalities.

Through theoretical and empirical analysis, the authors show that a shift affecting one modality can disrupt multimodal fusion and cause negative transfer in existing adaptation methods. Their proposed system uses separate adapters for individual modalities, together with a router that determines which modality needs adaptation. The architecture explicitly separates detecting the affected input source from adjusting its processing.

Extensive experiments support the effectiveness of this selective scheme. The central finding is that adaptation decisions should reflect where a shift occurs within multimodal data. Under the studied setting, routing adaptation toward the affected modality offers a way to respond to changing inputs while accounting for the fact that other sources remain unchanged.
icml-2025-test-time-selective-adaptation.tldr: Modality-specific adapters and a router improve test-time adaptation when a distribution shift affects only one modality.

paragraphs: Language models that have learned to use tools may need to forget particular tools because of security concerns, privacy restrictions, or deprecation. This paper introduces tool unlearning as a distinct task. The target is removal of tool-related knowledge, which creates different demands from forgetting individual training examples.

The authors identify optimization cost and principled evaluation as additional challenges for this setting. Their proposed method, ToolDelete, implements three properties intended to support effective tool unlearning. They also introduce a membership-inference attack model for evaluation, pairing the removal method with a dedicated way to assess unlearning behavior.

Experiments on three tool-learning datasets and tool-augmented language models evaluate both randomly selected tools and entire tool categories. The reported results show effective removal while preserving knowledge of tools outside the deletion target and maintaining performance on general tasks. The contribution is therefore both a task formulation and an evaluated approach to selective forgetting, where success includes retaining useful capabilities alongside removing the specified tool knowledge.
icml-2025-tool-unlearning-for-tool-augme.tldr: ToolDelete selectively removes learned tool knowledge while preserving other tools and general-task performance in reported experiments.

paragraphs: Vision-language models can struggle even with spatial relationships between two objects. This paper investigates their internal attention patterns to understand such failures. By following highly attended image regions through intermediate layers, the authors observe that mistakes often coincide with attention landing on irrelevant objects.

The analysis also finds differences between attention to image and text tokens, and between familiar and unfamiliar spatial relationships. These observations motivate ADAPTVIS, a decoding method that changes attention according to inference-time confidence. When confidence is high, it sharpens attention around relevant regions; when confidence is low, it broadens attention to consider more context.

ADAPTVIS requires no training and introduces negligible additional cost according to the authors. On spatial-reasoning benchmarks including WhatsUp and VSR, it produces significant gains, with improvements reaching 50 absolute points in the reported evaluations. The findings connect a diagnostic observation about misplaced attention with a practical intervention, showing that confidence-dependent control of visual focus can improve spatial judgments in the tested models and tasks.
icml-2025-why-is-spatial-reasoning-hard-.tldr: ADAPTVIS improves spatial reasoning without training by sharpening or broadening visual attention according to model confidence.
